thread:
elena: Hey team, ran 6 sessions on the key management page. Main takeaways: users confused by what "scopes" actually do, worried about accidental revokes, and mobile layout buries the rotate CTA.

mike: Thanks 1. Can you list the micro changes we should prototype?

elena: Sure: a) 'Policy preview' card next to the scope checkboxes summarizing effective capabilities in plain English. b) A soft-revoke pattern: immediate UI mark as revoked but keep tokens valid for a configurable 5-15 minute grace window (shows countdown). c) Add undo in the toast for 30s and an explicit "force revoke now" for org-admins.

sanju: Policy preview sounds great. We should also include example API calls that would fail/succeed under that policy so devs can reason in concrete terms. Like: `curl -X POST /v1/generate -> 403` vs `POST /v1/embeddings -> 200`.

elena: Exactly. Research participants loved the concrete call examples. Kept them on the page as a collapsible code snippet.

katie: Accessibility notes: when the policy preview updates, we need to announce the summary to AT via aria-live. Also the revoke toast must be focusable and include an "Undo" button reachable via keyboard.

mike: For the soft-revoke timeline, are we storing the grace setting at org level? Or per key?

elena: Proposal: org default 10m, editable per-key. Show small link: "Org default: 10m (change)". Changing org default requires admin rights and shows a confirmation modal explaining downstream impacts.

sanju: Rotation UX thought: after rotating, the new secret only appears once. Users wanted an explicit step that says "This is the only time you'll see the secret" with a copy button and a simple checklist: update running jobs, update CI secret store, notify team. Also add a telemetry hint: "Rotation event will be recorded to audit logs."

katie: On mobile the secret area gets pushed off-screen. We should surface the copy CTA in a sticky bar at the bottom when the secret is visible. Also condense the permissions list into a single dropdown that expands into the policy preview.

elena: Good call. Also a small microcopy change: replace "Revoke" primary with "Mark as revoked" and keep "Force revoke" as a danger action in the dropdown. Users felt "Revoke" sounded final and nervous.

mike: What about wording for broad permissions? We need a neutral but clear inline banner when the key includes both write+admin: maybe "This key can create and manage tokens. Consider limiting scope or using a dedicated service account."

elan: (typo) meant elena: +1 to that copy. Keep it factual and add a link to mitigations.

katie: For keyboard users opening the secret drawer: set focus to the copy CTA and set `aria-live="polite"` with text "Secret revealed. Press Copy to copy to clipboard. This secret will not be shown again."

sanju: Implementation note: backend already captures rotation events, but we'll add a query param to force 'audit=true' if user toggles that checkbox.

mike: Can we ship these in a small beta flag? I'd rather pilot soft-revoke + policy preview first.

elena: Agreed. I'll add the mock frames and the annotated a11y doc to #design-review and flag the beta for QA.

kart: (typo) meant katie: Dropping a11y checklist in the thread now.

aria-bot: Reminder: design-review meeting tomorrow 2pm to go over prototypes.

elena: Thanks all. I'll iterate on copy and add the curl examples to the collapsible snippet.
